## 1. Family architecture

Both models ship from the same release and differ primarily in scale [hf-pro-card, hf-flash-card]:

| Dimension | V4-Pro | V4-Flash |
|---|---|---|
| Total / active parameters | 1.6T / 49B | 284B / 13B |
| Context window | 1M tokens | 1M tokens |
| Precision | FP4 (MoE) + FP8 (rest) | FP4 (MoE) + FP8 (rest) |
| Reasoning modes | Non-think, Think High, Think Max | Non-think, Think High, Think Max |
| License | MIT | MIT |
| AA Intelligence Index | 52 (rank #3 of 77) | 47 (rank #9 of 77) |

Both expose OpenAI ChatCompletions and an Anthropic-format endpoint at `https://api.deepseek.com/anthropic` [deepseek-coding-agents-guide]. Both share identical sampling defaults (`temperature=1.0`, `top_p=1.0`) and 384K minimum-context for Think Max mode [hf-pro-card, hf-flash-card]. Architecturally both use Compressed Sparse Attention plus Heavily Compressed Attention, Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections, and Muon-optimizer training [hf-pro-card, hf-blog]. AA describes Flash as *"near Claude Sonnet 4.6 capability level"* [aa-overview].

## 2. Price ratio

DeepSeek's official pricing page lists the following per-1M-token rates [api-docs-pricing]:

| Model | Input cache miss | Output |
|---|---|---|
| `deepseek-v4-pro` (standard, post-2026-05-05) | $1.74 | $3.48 |
| `deepseek-v4-pro` (PROMO until 2026-05-05 15:59 UTC, 75% off) | $0.435 | $0.87 |
| `deepseek-v4-flash` | $0.14 | $0.28 |

**Output-token ratio:** Standard $3.48 / $0.28 = **12.4× more expensive on Pro**. Promo $0.87 / $0.28 = **~3.1×**. After 2026-05-05 15:59 UTC the ratio reverts to 12.4× [api-docs-pricing, thenextweb].

The 12.4× factor is the load-bearing number for routing economics — at that ratio, Pro must avoid >12 Flash retries or deliver enough quality lift per call to be worth it. During the promo window the breakeven tilts heavily toward Pro (only ~3 Flash retries justify the spend).

## 3. Quality-gap table

Per the Hugging Face model cards, with both models in their Max-effort reasoning mode [hf-pro-card, hf-flash-card]:

| Benchmark | V4-Pro | V4-Flash | Gap | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SWE-bench Verified | 80.6% | 79.0% | 1.6 pp | hf-pro-card, hf-flash-card |
| LiveCodeBench | 93.5% | 91.6% | 1.9 pp | hf-pro-card, hf-flash-card |
| MMLU-Pro | 87.5% | 86.2% | 1.3 pp | hf-pro-card, hf-flash-card |
| Codeforces (rating) | 3206 | 3052 | 154 pts | hf-pro-card, hf-flash-card |
| GPQA Diamond | 90.1% | 88.1% | 2.0 pp | hf-pro-card, hf-flash-card |
| Terminal-Bench 2.0 | 67.9% | 56.9% | **11 pp** | hf-pro-card, hf-flash-card, wavespeed |
| SimpleQA-Verified | 57.9% | 34.1% | **23.8 pp** | hf-pro-card, hf-flash-card, wavespeed |

The gap profile is bimodal: code/math/general-knowledge benchmarks all fall inside a 1-2 pp band, while agentic tool use (Terminal-Bench 2.0) and long-tail factual recall (SimpleQA-Verified) blow out to 11 pp and 23.8 pp respectively. WaveSpeed states this directly: *"Flash takes a real hit on both"* factual tasks and complex agentic work, while coding and math stay *"within striking distance"* [wavespeed-pro-vs-flash].

## 4. Routing implications from the gap data

1. **Coding (1-2 pp):** Flash is competitive. Paying 12.4× for ~2 pp on SWE-bench Verified is rarely worth it on per-PR economics — that gap is inside the noise band of most codebases [hf-flash-card, wavespeed].
2. **Multi-step agentic loops (11 pp Terminal-Bench):** Pro is materially better. An 11 pp success-rate lift compounds across a 5-step tool chain — the Pro premium is justified once tool-use failures dominate [hf-flash-card, wavespeed].
3. **Long-tail factual recall (23.8 pp SimpleQA-Verified):** Pro is materially better. AA also flags that *"V4 Pro and V4 Flash both have a very high hallucination rate of 94% and 96% respectively"* [aa-overview] — both confabulate when uncertain, but Pro is correct far more often when it does know.

## 5. WaveSpeed production routing guide

WaveSpeed's per-task recommendations [wavespeed-pro-vs-flash]:

- **V4-Flash for:** high-throughput classification and tagging, summarization and translation, interactive chat, query rewriting, intent classification.
- **V4-Pro for:** multi-step agent loops with tool orchestration, factual accuracy on long-tail entities, enterprise correctness, extended reasoning across full 1M-token contexts.

Recommended architecture: *"Default requests to Flash. Escalate to Pro on explicit triggers (tool failures, confidence thresholds, multi-turn agent complexity)"* [wavespeed]. Tune by escalation rate: *"under 5% suggests Flash adequacy. Above 30% indicates Pro-primary workloads"* [wavespeed]. The 5-30% band is where dynamic routing earns its complexity; outside it, a static split is fine.

## 6. Latency and throughput

Per Artificial Analysis measurements [aa-pro-model, aa-flash-model]:

| Metric | V4-Pro | V4-Flash | Flash advantage |
|---|---|---|---|
| Time-to-First-Token | 2.02 s | 1.03 s | 2.0× faster |
| Output throughput | 38.5 t/s (rank #39) | 82.7 t/s (well above 56.5 t/s median) | 2.15× faster |

Pro is below the 56.5 t/s AA-platform median [aa-pro-model], which matters for user-facing latency. Flash's TTFT-and-throughput combination makes it the obvious choice for chat UIs and short-turn interactive workloads.

## 7. Slotting into existing multi-tier setups

Anthropic's own Sonnet/Haiku output-price ratio is roughly 12× — close to the 12.4× V4-Pro/V4-Flash standard ratio — which makes a one-for-one substitution natural. DeepSeek's official Coding-Agents Integration Guide gives the recommended Claude Code mapping verbatim [deepseek-coding-agents-guide]:

```
ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL=deepseek-v4-pro
ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL=deepseek-v4-pro
ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL=deepseek-v4-flash
CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL=deepseek-v4-flash
CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL=max
```

Two takeaways: (1) Pro fills both Opus and Sonnet slots, Flash fills Haiku and subagents — a static split, no dynamic router required [deepseek-coding-agents-guide]. (2) DeepSeek positions Pro as Sonnet/Opus equivalent and Flash as Haiku equivalent. AA's framing of Flash as *"near Claude Sonnet 4.6 capability level"* [aa-overview] is more aggressive than DeepSeek's own mapping, suggesting Flash may be underused if reflexively assigned only to Haiku-level work.

## 8. AA cost per benchmark suite

AA published end-to-end Intelligence Index suite costs [aa-overview]: **V4-Pro $1,071** (190M output tokens), **V4-Flash $113** (240M output tokens). Ratio **9.5×**, smaller than the 12.4× headline because Flash is more verbose — verbosity erodes some of Flash's per-token cost advantage. Takeaway: model spend on tokens-out, not requests, and assume Flash produces more output per task than Pro. AA also notes V4-Pro is *"4x cheaper than Claude Opus"* on the same suite [aa-overview].

## 9. Recommendation for individual / small team

Decision tree, simplest-first:

1. **Default to Flash.** At $0.14/$0.28 per 1M tokens with Sonnet-class capability and 2× faster TTFT [aa-flash-model, api-docs-pricing], Flash is the right default for code generation, chat, summarization, ad-hoc tasks.
2. **Escalate to Pro on agentic loops.** Pro's 11 pp Terminal-Bench lead [hf-flash-card] compounds across multi-step tool use. Use WaveSpeed triggers (tool failures, confidence thresholds, multi-turn complexity) [wavespeed].
3. **Escalate to Pro on factual workloads.** SimpleQA-Verified gap is 23.8 pp [hf-flash-card]. Pair Pro with retrieval grounding.
4. **During promo (until 2026-05-05 15:59 UTC):** Pro at $0.87 output is competitively priced — ~3.1× Flash rather than 12.4× [api-docs-pricing]. The moment to test Pro-primary configurations on heavy reasoning workloads.
5. **Simplest static split:** the DeepSeek-recommended Claude Code env-var mapping [deepseek-coding-agents-guide]. Pro for primary, Flash for subagents. No router required.
6. **Skip RouteLLM-class dynamic routing.** Most individual workloads sit outside the 5-30% escalation band [wavespeed], where a static split captures most of the value. Dynamic routing pays off only in that band at non-trivial scale.

Instrument the escalation-rate metric (5% / 30% bands) and tune the static split by what you observe. Re-evaluate after 2026-05-05 when the price ratio snaps back to 12.4×.
